chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a mawla (freedman/companion) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from the people of Medina, who said:
I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) begin the Sa'ee from the house of Al-Qazi Al-Makhzoumi. He said, 'And he continued as he was, up to the alleyway of the perfume sellers.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam Al-Reza, peace be upon him)
key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'ee (ritual walking between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: Where did Imam Al-Reza begin the Sa'ee ritual according to this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a specific historical precedent for the Sa'ee ritual, linking the physical act of circumambulation to the domestic and social geography of Medina during the time of Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him). It highlights the scholarly tradition of deriving legal rulings (fiqh) from the precise movements of the Imams, emphasizing that the ritual's validity is tied to following their established path and manner of performance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a friend of Abu Abdullahasws, from the people of Al Medina who said,

‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> beginning the Sa’ee from the door of Al-Qazy Al-Makhzoumy’. He said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> went on just as he<sup>asws</sup> was, up to the alleyway of the perfume sellers’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Mawla’ abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, from people of al-Madinah who has said the following: “

I saw abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, perform Sa‘y (walking faster like running slowly) from the house of al-Qadiy al-Makhzumiy.’ He has said that he (the Imam) continued until he reached the lane of al-‘Attarin (perfume sellers).”’
